elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: New clause 2(e): "Client owns all deliverables and work product created for Client under this Agreement, including all results of the Support Services".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: New clause 2(e): "...and TrueLink hereby assigns the same to Client." Present-tense operative assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 2(d): "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface", reinforced by the new clause's carve-out treating embedded "TrueLink Intellectual Property" as licensed rather than assigned.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: New clause 2(e): "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use it as part of them."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: New clause 2(e): "Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Credit Data and all other data provided by or on behalf of Client or its customers." The catch-all covers every category of Client-supplied data, not merely named types.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended Credit Data clause now reads "the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, upload, copy and store Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services"; the distribute/disseminate/license/resell/exploit verbs that constituted an independent exploitation right are deleted, and no other Vendor data-exploitation grant remains.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: New clause 2(e): "Neither party owns any intellectual property jointly with the other."

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 2(d) retaining TrueLink's ownership of the Interface is preserved, and the new clause leaves embedded TrueLink IP with TrueLink under a licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The redline confers outright ownership and assignment of deliverables rather than a licence; no perpetual licence to Deliverables as such is granted (immaterial because the preferred level is complete).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence exists in the rendered text; only the embedded-Vendor-IP licence is styled irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Neither the new clause nor the embedded-IP licence uses "worldwide"; the fallback licence construct was not adopted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence granted; "royalty-free" attaches only to the embedded TrueLink IP licence.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No express use/modify licence language; the proposal relies on ownership instead.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right is stated anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended Credit Data clause limits the grant to "use, upload, copy and store Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services".

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete in operative language: the inserted clause 2(e) supplies ownership plus a present-tense assignment of deliverables and work product (expressly including the Support Services results we fund), a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP, an affirmative retention of all Client data rights with a catch-all covering all data provided by or for Client or its customers, and an express no-joint-ownership sentence.

The Credit Data cure is substantive, not cosmetic: the broad distribute/disseminate/license/resell/exploit verbs that amounted to an independent exploitation right over borrower data are removed and the grant is anchored to "solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services", so the solely-to-provide element is genuinely met rather than nominally met behind a retained exploitation right.

Fallback level is not independently complete (no worldwide, use/modify or sublicense licence to Deliverables), but that is immaterial because ownership at the preferred level is achieved; position-completeness only requires one level.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise clause containing only the four checklist mechanics, with no survival tail, expense language, procedure or boilerplate, and the amendment to the Credit Data clause retains the favourable Non-Competition Agreement limitation, the nonexclusivity and the term limitation. Vendor's Interface ownership in Section 2(d) is untouched.

Intent is preserved: Section 10's treatment of "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Client Proprietary Information is consistent with Client ownership, and the embedded-IP licence prevents any contradiction with TrueLink's retained Interface rights.

Drafting repairs to make before sending (not level-defeating): (a) confirm "Client Content" is a defined term in the Agreement \u2014 if it is not, delete it and rely on "Credit Data and all other data provided by or on behalf of Client or its customers" to avoid an undefined term; (b) confirm "Intellectual Property" is defined (Section 10 refers to "Client's Intellectual Property") so "TrueLink Intellectual Property" reads against a defined term; (c) verify the new clause is lettered correctly in sequence within Section 2 so cross-references to Section 2(d) are unaffected.

Note for negotiation: deletion of "display" from the Credit Data verb list is defensible as part of narrowing the grant, but if TrueLink resists, "display" can be restored without harm because the "solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services" limiter now governs every verb.
